items.name: tokens
items.title: Semantic tokens
items.description: The color, type, space, shape and motion custom properties every block reads, with neutral defaults.
items.useWhen: A project has no theme yet and you want one place to set colors, fonts, type scale, spacing and radius for every block.
items.avoidWhen: The site already defines these roles, as every Site Boulder starter does. Keep the site's own tokens.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: A link or button with solid, outline and quiet variants that read the accent, radius and action-weight tokens.
items.useWhen: You need consistent primary and secondary actions across sections.
items.avoidWhen: A plain text link reads better, such as inside running prose.

props.name: variant
props.description: solid: filled with the accent. outline: a quiet border in the current text color. quiet: an underlined text link with an arrow.

props.name: href
props.description: Renders a link. Omit it to render a button.

items.usage: --- import Button from "../components/ui/Button.astro"; ---

items.name: header-floating
items.title: Floating header
items.description: A detached, rounded navigation bar that floats below the top edge with a translucent surface and a native popover menu on narrow screens.
items.useWhen: The site has four to six destinations plus one primary action, and the page below has imagery or color the bar can float over.
items.avoidWhen: The site is a quiet single page, or the brand needs a large masthead. Use header-minimal or header-editorial instead.

props.name: brand
props.description: Site name. Used as the home link text, or as the logo's alt text.

props.name: logo
props.type: { src: string; alt?: string; width?: number; height?: number }

props.name: action
props.description: One primary action. It sits in the bar and moves into the menu on the narrowest screens.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Keep the bar pinned below the top edge while scrolling.

props.name: menuId
props.description: Unique id for the narrow-screen menu when a page has two headers.

items.name: header-editorial
items.title: Editorial header
items.description: A magazine masthead: a centered wordmark with tagline, a top line for an issue or place, and section links between double rules that wrap instead of hiding.
items.useWhen: The site publishes writing or has distinct sections, and the name deserves to be the loudest thing at the top.
items.avoidWhen: The site needs a primary action in the header more than a wordmark, or the name is long. Use header-floating or header-minimal.

props.name: brand
props.description: Publication or site name, set as a large centered wordmark.

props.name: logo
props.type: { src: string; alt?: string; width?: number; height?: number }

props.name: tagline
props.description: One line under the wordmark, such as what the publication covers.

props.name: meta
props.description: A short line at the top left, such as an issue, date or place.

props.name: links
props.description: Sections. They stay visible and wrap onto more lines on narrow screens.

props.name: action
props.description: One action at the top right, such as Subscribe.

items.usage:
---
import HeaderEditorial from "../components/blocks/HeaderEditorial.astro";
import HeroTypographic from "../components/blocks/HeroTypographic.astro";
---

<HeaderEditorial
  brand="Kestrel Review"
  tagline="Essays, fiction and criticism from the Pacific Northwest"
  meta="Issue 42 · Autumn 2026"
  links={[
    { label: "Essays", href: "/essays" },
    { label: "Fiction", href: "/fiction" },
    { label: "Poetry", href: "/poetry" },
    { label: "Interviews", href: "/interviews" },
    { label: "Archive", href: "/archive" },
  ]}
  action={{ label: "Subscribe", href: "/subscribe" }}
/>
<main style="inline-size: min(72rem, 100% - 2.5rem); margin-inline: auto;">
  <HeroTypographic
    title="The quiet economy of small presses"
    emphasis="small presses"
    lede="How a dozen two-person publishers keep regional writing in print, told by the people who run them."
    actions={[{ label: "Read the lead essay", href: "/essays/small-presses" }]}
    align="center"
    headingLevel={1}
  />
</main>

items.name: header-transparent
items.title: Transparent header
items.description: A header that overlays the opening image in light or dark ink, with a native popover menu on narrow screens and, where supported, a solid surface that fades in while scrolling.
items.useWhen: The page opens with a full-bleed photograph or artwork that should start at the very top.
items.avoidWhen: The opening is text on a plain background, or the image is busy where the header sits. Use header-minimal or header-floating.

props.name: brand
props.description: Site name. Used as the home link text, or as the logo's alt text.

props.name: logo
props.type: { src: string; alt?: string; width?: number; height?: number }

props.name: tone
props.description: light: white text for dark imagery. dark: text color for light imagery.

props.name: solidOnScroll
props.description: Pin the header and fade in a solid surface while scrolling, where the browser supports scroll-driven animation.

props.name: menuId
props.description: Unique id for the narrow-screen menu when a page has two headers.

items.name: header-minimal
items.title: Minimal header
items.description: A single quiet row: name, two to five links and an optional action. Links wrap onto their own row on narrow screens instead of hiding in a menu.
items.useWhen: There are only a few destinations and every one should stay visible, especially on phones.
items.avoidWhen: There are more than five links, or the header should overlay imagery.

props.name: brand
props.description: Site name. Used as the home link text, or as the logo's alt text.

props.name: logo
props.type: { src: string; alt?: string; width?: number; height?: number }

props.name: links
props.description: Two to five links. They wrap onto their own row on narrow screens instead of hiding in a menu.

props.name: divider
props.description: Draw a hairline under the header.

items.name: hero-split
items.title: Split hero
items.description: Headline, lede and actions beside one framed image or artwork, stacking copy-first on narrow screens.
items.useWhen: There is one strong, real image or artwork that shows the actual work, and a clear first action.
items.avoidWhen: There is no genuine image. Use hero-typographic rather than a stock or decorative picture.

props.name: actions
props.description: The first action is the primary one; keep it to one or two.

props.name: image
props.type: { src: string; alt: string; width?: number; height?: number }
props.description: One real image. Use the media slot instead for a picture, video or SVG artwork.

props.name: ratio
props.description: CSS aspect-ratio of the media frame on wide screens.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of the copy against the media.

items.usage:
--- import HeroSplit from "../components/blocks/HeroSplit.astro"; ---

Same-week appointments · Most insurance accepted

items.name: hero-immersive
items.title: Immersive hero
items.description: A full-bleed photograph or artwork with the headline, lede and actions set in white over a contrast-safe gradient scrim.
items.useWhen: There is a striking, high-quality photograph or artwork of the real place, product or experience.
items.avoidWhen: The image is a stock photo, low resolution, or bright across the bottom third. Use hero-split, which frames the image beside the text.

props.name: image
props.type: { src: string; alt: string; width?: number; height?: number }
props.description: A full-bleed photograph or artwork. Use the media slot instead for a picture or video element.

props.name: position
props.description: CSS object-position for the image, to keep the subject in frame as the crop changes.

props.name: scrim
props.description: How strongly the image darkens behind the text. Keep strong unless the image is already dark at the bottom.

items.usage:
--- import HeroImmersive from "../components/blocks/HeroImmersive.astro"; ---

RYA recognised · April to October

items.name: hero-typographic
items.title: Typographic hero
items.description: A large statement headline with one accented phrase, an optional lede and actions, and a ruled row of short facts.
items.useWhen: The positioning sentence is the strongest material, or there is no imagery yet.
items.avoidWhen: The headline runs past about fourteen words, or a photo of the real work would say more.

props.name: title
props.description: One statement sentence. The headline is the hero, so keep it under about 14 words.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: A word or phrase from the title to set in the accent color.

props.name: facts
props.description: Two to four short facts shown on a ruled line, such as place, hours or founding year.

items.name: steps-numbered
items.title: Numbered steps
items.description: An ordered list of two to five steps with large numerals, set side by side on wide screens or one per line for longer text.
items.useWhen: Visitors need to understand a real sequence, such as how booking, a project or a course of care unfolds.
items.avoidWhen: The items have no inherent order. Numbering unordered features is decoration; use features-editorial instead.

props.name: steps
props.description: Two to five steps of a real sequence. Numbers carry meaning here, so don't use this for unordered features.

props.name: layout
props.description: row: steps side by side on wide screens. list: one step per line, for longer step text.

types.Step: { title: string; text: string; detail?: string }

items.usage:
---
import StepsNumbered from "../components/blocks/StepsNumbered.astro";
---

<StepsNumbered
  title="How a course of care works"
  intro="One clinician sees you through every step, so you never repeat your story."
  steps={[
    { title: "Assessment", text: "A full hour to understand the injury, your history and what you want to get back to.", detail: "60 minutes" },
    { title: "Plan", text: "A written plan with milestones you can check yourself, not just a list of exercises.", detail: "Same day" },
    { title: "Treatment", text: "Hands-on sessions alongside a home programme sized to your week.", detail: "Weekly" },
    { title: "Review", text: "We retest against your first assessment and decide together when you are done.", detail: "At week six" },
  ]}
/>

items.name: timeline
items.title: Timeline
items.description: A vertical timeline of dated entries on a rail, with an optional current entry and labels in their own column on wide screens.
items.useWhen: Dates or phases carry the meaning: a company history, a project schedule or an event programme.
items.avoidWhen: There are fewer than three entries, or the dates add nothing. A paragraph is clearer.

props.name: items
props.description: Entries in order, oldest or first first.

types.Entry: { label: string; title: string; text?: string; current?: boolean }

items.usage:
---
import Timeline from "../components/blocks/Timeline.astro";
---

<Timeline
  title="From one borrowed oven to four"
  intro="Quarry Bread grew one bake at a time."
  items={[
    { label: "2016", title: "A borrowed oven", text: "Weekend loaves baked overnight in a friend's restaurant kitchen and sold from a market table." },
    { label: "2018", title: "Mill Lane opens", text: "Our own shop and a wood-fired deck oven, open four mornings a week." },
    { label: "2021", title: "Wholesale", text: "Bread for twelve cafés within cycling distance, delivered before seven." },
    { label: "Now", title: "A second bakery", text: "A night-bake kitchen across town so the shop can open every day.", current: true },
  ]}
/>

items.name: alternating-rows
items.title: Alternating rows
items.description: Rows that pair an image, or a large typographic figure, with a short text, alternating sides on wide screens.
items.useWhen: Each point has its own real image or one striking number, and the points read in order.
items.avoidWhen: The rows would all use similar stock images, or there are more than five rows.

props.name: start
props.description: Which side the first row's media sits on wide screens.

props.name: ratio
props.description: CSS aspect-ratio of each media frame.

types.Row: { title: string; text: string; image?: { src: string; alt: string; width?: number; height?: number }; figure?: string; figureLabel?: string; link?: { label: string; href: string } }

items.name: features-bento
items.title: Bento features
items.description: An asymmetric grid of related features with one large tile, wide and tall tiles, accent and outline tones, and whole-tile links.
items.useWhen: Four to seven related capabilities differ in importance, and one deserves the largest tile.
items.avoidWhen: The items are unrelated, equal in weight, or exactly three. A bento grid of unrelated boxes reads as filler; use features-editorial.

props.name: items
props.description: Four to seven related items of different weight. Give the most important one size large. On wide screens a row holds four cells: large fills four (two by two), wide and tall two, default one, so pick sizes that fill whole rows.

types.Tile: { title: string; text?: string; label?: string; image?: { src: string; alt: string; width?: number; height?: number }; size?: "default" | "large" | "wide" | "tall"; tone?: "surface" | "accent" | "outline"; href?: string }

items.usage:
---
import FeaturesBento from "../components/blocks/FeaturesBento.astro";
---

<FeaturesBento
  title="What Orbit does each week"
  intro="Everything below runs automatically once your events are connected."
  items={[
    {
      title: "One plain-language report",
      text: "Every Monday, the five changes that matter, written as sentences your whole team can act on.",
      image: { src: "/gallery/field.svg", alt: "Abstract green fields under a yellow sun", width: 1200, height: 900 },
      size: "large",
      href: "/sample",
    },
    { label: "Saved per analyst each week", title: "4.2 hours", tone: "accent" },
    { label: "Audited every year", title: "SOC 2", tone: "outline" },
    { title: "Alerts that explain themselves", text: "Every alert names the segment, the size of the change and its likely cause, so nobody has to dig.", size: "wide" },
  ]}
/>

items.name: features-editorial
items.title: Editorial features
items.description: A large heading and intro that stay in view beside a ruled list of offers, each with a title, a sentence or two and an optional label.
items.useWhen: Services or offers need a sentence each, and reading them in order matters more than visual variety.
items.avoidWhen: There are only one or two items, or each needs an image. Use alternating-rows.

props.name: items
props.description: Three to seven offers or services, each with a sentence or two.

types.Item: { title: string; text: string; label?: string; href?: string }

items.usage:
---
import FeaturesEditorial from "../components/blocks/FeaturesEditorial.astro";
---

<FeaturesEditorial
  title="What we treat"
  intro="Most people come to us with one of these. If yours isn't here, ask; we will tell you honestly if we are the right clinic."
  action={{ label: "Ask about your injury", href: "/contact" }}
  items={[
    { title: "Sports injuries", text: "Sprains, strains and overuse injuries, with a return-to-play plan you can test yourself against.", label: "Most common" },
    { title: "Back and neck pain", text: "Assessment of posture, load and work habits alongside hands-on treatment.", href: "/back-pain" },
    { title: "After surgery", text: "Rehabilitation after joint replacement or ligament repair, coordinated with your surgeon." },
    { title: "Pelvic health", text: "Pre- and postnatal care with a specialist clinician in a private room.", label: "Women's health" },
  ]}
/>

items.name: footer-minimal
items.title: Minimal footer
items.description: One quiet line: copyright, a short note such as an address or hours, a few links and an optional credit.
items.useWhen: The site is small, and the footer only needs to answer where, when and who.
items.avoidWhen: The site has many pages that visitors look for at the bottom. Use footer-columns.

props.name: note
props.description: One short line, such as an address or opening hours.

props.name: credit
props.description: A small credit link kept at the end of the row, such as the site builder's.

props.name: year
props.description: The copyright year. Defaults to the current year.

items.name: footer-columns
items.title: Column footer
items.description: A brand block with description and action beside titled link columns, over a bottom bar for copyright, legal links and a credit.
items.useWhen: The site has enough pages that a footer sitemap genuinely helps visitors.
items.avoidWhen: There are fewer than six links in total. Use footer-minimal.

props.name: description
props.description: One or two sentences about the organization.

props.name: columns
props.description: Two to four titled groups of links.

props.name: legal
props.description: Small links in the bottom bar, such as privacy and terms.

props.name: credit
props.description: A small credit link kept in the bottom bar, such as the site builder's.

items.name: footer-wordmark
items.title: Wordmark footer
items.description: Footer links and a note above the site name set across the full width, sized from its length, with an inverse or plain tone.
items.useWhen: The name is short and the rest of the site is quiet, so the footer can be the one expressive brand moment.
items.avoidWhen: The header already shows a large wordmark, or the name runs past about sixteen characters. A repeated giant wordmark reads as filler.

props.name: name
props.description: A short name. It is set across the full width, so names over about 16 characters get small.

props.name: credit
props.description: A small credit link kept in the bottom row, such as the site builder's.

props.name: fit
props.description: Share of the width the name should fill. Lower it if a wide display face overflows.

items.usage:
---
import FooterWordmark from "../components/blocks/FooterWordmark.astro";
---

<FooterWordmark
  name="Fernhill"
  note="An architecture studio for homes and small workplaces, in Bristol and by appointment."
  links={[
    { label: "Work", href: "/work" },
    { label: "Practice", href: "/practice" },
    { label: "Journal", href: "/journal" },
    { label: "Contact", href: "/contact" },
  ]}
/>

items.name: footer-cta
items.title: Call-to-action footer
items.description: A closing band with one invitation and up to two actions, merged with a compact footer row, in inverse, accent or surface tone.
items.useWhen: Every page should end by offering the same next step, such as booking or getting in touch.
items.avoidWhen: The page already ends with a strong call to action, or there is no concrete next step to offer.

props.name: title
props.description: The closing invitation, named by what actually happens next.

props.name: actions
props.description: One or two actions; the first is primary.

props.name: credit
props.description: A small credit link kept in the bottom row, such as the site builder's.
